title: Sub-mesh mutual-guarantee pools: does local pooling fix the routine-friction failure without recreating a centre? (pre-registered and hash-locked BEFORE any implementation existed)
the_failure_this_addresses: The Reciprocal Settlement Mesh (spec a5f49a6e) scored 2/5. Its reserve invariant held over 200,000 operations and all six named attacks were blocked, but it lost the shared-shock replay badly: 2,458 failed settlements against a centralised comparator's 0, on an identical 4,886 real-shock sequence with no architecture-specific constants. The diagnosis was pooling: a central balance sheet holds every issuer's reserves and can meet obligations no isolated node could. A pure mesh has no pool. The proposed remedy is to pool LOCALLY -- k-neighbour clusters holding a capped mutual-guarantee reserve -- so that routine timing mismatches are absorbed without any single entity intermediating the whole network.
the_simulation_trap_being_avoided_again: IMPORTANT. A published JAX cell for this proposal computes friction as friction_absorption = exp(-0.15 * (k - 1)) and blast radius as k / total_nodes, then plots the result. Both outputs are written into the two expressions; no settlement is simulated, no shock is replayed, and the 'optimal zone' is a property of the chosen exponential. This is the sixth appearance of the tuned-formula pattern in this project. Here, pooling is IMPLEMENTED inside the same settlement engine already built and attacked, driven by the SAME committed real shock sequence, and the friction and blast-radius numbers are MEASURED outputs of that engine rather than closed-form expressions. If local pooling does not help, the runs will say so.

what_is_being_added_to_the_mechanism.cluster: The n nodes are partitioned into disjoint clusters of size k. Clustering is structural and fixed before any shock is replayed.
what_is_being_added_to_the_mechanism.mutual_guarantee_pool: Each cluster holds a pool funded by its members transferring a fixed fraction of their OWN existing reserves into it. Total system reserves are unchanged by pooling -- value is moved, never created. This is the property S1 and S4 exist to check.
what_is_being_added_to_the_mechanism.draw_rule: A member facing a settlement shortfall may draw from its cluster pool, capped at the pool's actual balance and at the member's own contributed share multiplied by a fixed cap factor. Draws are no-recourse: an unrepaid draw is absorbed proportionally by the cluster, never by the wider network.
what_is_being_added_to_the_mechanism.blast_radius: The share of the network exposed to the failure of any single pooling entity, measured as the largest cluster's size divided by n. For a pure mesh this is 1/n; for a single global pool it is 1.

fixed_parameters.note: Carried over unchanged from spec a5f49a6e wherever they overlap, so results are comparable across specs. The k sweep is the independent variable. No parameter may differ between k settings other than k itself.

gates.S1_pooling_does_not_create_value: Total system reserves after clustering and pooling must equal total system reserves before, to within floating-point tolerance, at every k. PASS iff the maximum absolute discrepancy across the whole sweep is below 1e-6. CAN FAIL -- an accounting error in the pool would silently create claims, which is precisely the failure mode the whole architecture exists to prevent.
gates.S2_local_pooling_reduces_routine_frictio: There must exist at least one cluster size k > 1 whose failed-settlement count is strictly lower than the pure mesh (k = 1) under the identical real shock replay. PASS iff such a k exists. FALSIFIABLE AND AT GENUINE RISK: local pools are small, and a cluster whose members are shocked together has nothing to lend. If no k helps, local pooling does not solve the friction problem and that is the reported result.
gates.S3_an_operating_zone_exists_that_is_both: THE CENTRAL CLAIM OF THE PROPOSAL, made falsifiable. There must exist a cluster size k satisfying BOTH conditions simultaneously: failed settlements below 50% of the pure-mesh baseline, AND blast radius below 0.10. PASS iff such a k exists. CAN FAIL -- the two objectives are in direct tension, since larger clusters absorb more friction and expose more of the network. A failure means no operating zone exists at these parameters and the proposal does not deliver what it claims.
gates.S4_no_draw_exceeds_what_the_pool_actuall: Instrument every draw and assert that no draw exceeds the pool's balance at that moment, and that no pool balance ever goes negative. PASS iff zero violations across the entire sweep. CAN FAIL. This is the operational form of the no-credit-creation rule.
gates.S5_the_published_k20_prediction_is_teste: The proposal states that a cluster of 20 nodes drops settlement failures by over 90% while holding blast radius to about 0.02. Both halves are checked against the measured run at k = 20. PASS iff the measured failure reduction exceeds 90% AND the measured blast radius is at most 0.02. FALSIFIABLE BOTH WAYS and reported at full force either way -- the prediction was made before this test existed, and a miss is a miss.
gates.S6_the_blast_radius_ordering_is_monotone: Blast radius must increase weakly with cluster size across the sweep. PASS iff the measured sequence is non-decreasing. DECLARED close to definitional given the measurement, so it is reported as a CONSISTENCY CHECK and EXCLUDED from the score.
gates.S7_no_architecture_specific_constant_dif: Inspect the parameters actually used at each k and assert that only k differs. PASS iff no other key varies. DECLARED falsifiable:false, EXCLUDED from the score. It exists so the tuned-formula pattern cannot recur, and it is the gate the published JAX cell would fail.
gates.S8_no_theological_or_arabic_terminology_: Scan the implementation against the same fixed term list used in spec a5f49a6e. PASS iff none appears. DECLARED falsifiable:false, EXCLUDED from the score, enforcing the standing terminology directive.

symmetric_null: Every failure count, blast radius and reserve total is reported with its exact value whether or not it favours the proposal. S2, S3 and S5 are genuinely at risk, and S5 tests a specific published prediction that may simply be wrong. S1 and S4 are pass/fail properties the implementation can violate. S6, S7 and S8 are excluded from the score. No parameter in this file may move after the lock, and no result may be rescued by adding a per-k constant.
what_a_pass_would_and_would_not_mean: Passing S1-S5 would establish that local mutual-guarantee pools, implemented inside the same settlement engine already attacked, absorb a measurable share of routine friction under a real recorded shock sequence while holding the blast radius below a stated bound, without creating value. It would NOT establish that such pools are legally permissible, that members would join them, that cluster membership could be assigned in practice, that the pools survive correlated shocks hitting a whole cluster, or anything at all about the world. No such system has been deployed and simulating a design is not evidence about reality.
acceptance: GREEN when this spec re-hashes to its published canonical SHA-256, the shock source matches its committed hash, and every gate is evaluated exactly as written -- with misses recorded and the published k=20 prediction reported as measured. Exit 0 means 'reproduces including its failures', never 'sub-mesh pooling works'.
